claim: An agent-based model extends earlier 'strain theory' by addressing the var gene family of Plasmodium falciparum.
source: An agent-based model is developed that extends earlier 'strain theory' by addressing the var gene family of Plasmodium falciparum.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the development of the model and its purpose.

claim: The model explicitly considers the extensive diversity of multi-copy genes that undergo antigenic variation via sequential, mutually exclusive expression.
source: The model explicitly considers the extensive diversity of multi-copy genes that undergo antigenic variation via sequential, mutually exclusive expression.
evidence: The abstract describes the model's features.

claim: Even under high levels of sexual recombination, strain competition mediated through cross-immunity structures the parasite population into a subset of coexisting dominant repertoires of var genes.
source: It tracks the dynamics of all unique var repertoires in a population of hosts, and shows that even under high levels of sexual recombination, strain competition mediated through cross-immunity structures the parasite population into a subset of coexisting dominant repertoires of var genes whose degree of antigenic overlap depends on transmission intensity.
evidence: The abstract presents the main finding from the model.

claim: The degree of antigenic overlap between dominant var gene repertoires depends on transmission intensity.
source: It tracks the dynamics of all unique var repertoires in a population of hosts, and shows that even under high levels of sexual recombination, strain competition mediated through cross-immunity structures the parasite population into a subset of coexisting dominant repertoires of var genes whose degree of antigenic overlap depends on transmission intensity.
evidence: The abstract states this relationship explicitly.

claim: Empirical comparison of patterns of genetic variation at antigenic and neutral sites supports the role for immune selection in structuring parasite diversity.
source: Empirical comparison of patterns of genetic variation at antigenic and neutral sites supports this role for immune selection in structuring parasite diversity.
evidence: The abstract presents empirical support for the model's predictions.

claim: Many pathogen populations are composed of several independent strains.
source: Many pathogen populations seem to be composed of several independent strains; this has important implications for disease surveillance and control, as well as for the identification of vaccine targets.
evidence: The introduction presents this as an established observation.

claim: Population genetic interactions between pathogen strains can influence transmissibility, clinical immunity, and the duration and severity of infection.
source: In particular, the population genetic interactions between pathogen strains can have significant epidemiological consequences, influencing transmissibility, clinical immunity, and the duration and severity of infection.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: An extensive variety of microparasites have been studied in the context of strain structure, including protozoa, viruses, and bacteria.
source: An extensive variety of microparasites have been studied in this context: protozoa, such as Plasmodium falciparum, Leishmania, and Trypanosoma brucei; viruses, such as Influenza, HIV and Dengue; and bacteria, such as E. coli, Bordetella spp. and Neisseria meningitides (Tibayrenc et al., 1990; Gupta et al., 1994; Tibayrenc and Ayala, 2002).
evidence: The introduction cites literature on various microparasites studied for strain structure.

claim: Mathematical models have demonstrated that immune selection can lead to the maintenance of discrete, non-overlapping, antigenic repertoires even when antigenic variability is driven by several unlinked genes that undergo recombination.
source: In particular, while it would seem that sufficient out-crossing should always lead to random associations between alleles (Tibayrenc et al., 1990; Tibayrenc and Ayala, 2002) and preclude the persistence of 'independently transmitted strains' (Tibayrenc, 1994), mathematical models of competition between pathogen strains have demonstrated that immune selection can lead to the maintenance of discrete, non-overlapping, antigenic repertoires—even when antigenic variability is driven by several unlinked genes that undergo recombination (Gupta et al., 1996; Gupta and Anderson, 1999).
evidence: The introduction cites previous mathematical modeling work.

claim: P. falciparum is responsible for the deadliest type of malaria in humans.
source: P. falciparum is responsible for the deadliest type of malaria in humans.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: The var genes encode P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1), the major surface antigen of the parasite's blood stages.
source: The var genes encode P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1)—the major surface antigen of the parasite's blood stages that binds to host endothelial cell receptors to allow the parasite to sequester within various host tissues (Miller et al., 2002; Scherf et al., 2008).
evidence: The introduction cites literature on var gene function.

claim: PfEMP1 binds to host endothelial cell receptors to allow the parasite to sequester within various host tissues.
source: The var genes encode P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1)—the major surface antigen of the parasite's blood stages that binds to host endothelial cell receptors to allow the parasite to sequester within various host tissues (Miller et al., 2002; Scherf et al., 2008).
evidence: The introduction cites literature on PfEMP1 function.

claim: Var genes are composed of multiple Duffy-binding-like (DBL) and cysteine-interdomain-rich (CIDR) domains that encode binding functions for specific endothelial receptors.
source: Var genes are composed of multiple Duffy-binding-like (DBL) and cysteine-interdomain-rich (CIDR) domains that encode binding functions for specific endothelial receptors.
evidence: The introduction describes the structure of var genes.

claim: DBLα is the only domain found in nearly all var genes.
source: DBLα, is the only domain found in nearly all var genes (Miller et al., 2002), and hence is the most informative molecular marker of var gene diversity.
evidence: The introduction cites literature on DBLα domain prevalence.

claim: DBLα is the most informative molecular marker of var gene diversity.
source: DBLα, is the only domain found in nearly all var genes (Miller et al., 2002), and hence is the most informative molecular marker of var gene diversity.
evidence: The introduction infers this from the prevalence of DBLα.

claim: Each parasite genome has up to 60 var genes.
source: Each parasite genome has up to 60 var genes, and differential sequential expression of these genes allows the parasite to evade the host immune response and establish a chronic infection.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: Differential sequential expression of var genes allows the parasite to evade the host immune response and establish a chronic infection.
source: Each parasite genome has up to 60 var genes, and differential sequential expression of these genes allows the parasite to evade the host immune response and establish a chronic infection.
evidence: The introduction states this as established knowledge.

claim: Clonal antigenic variation extends the duration of infection to facilitate transmission to the mosquito.
source: This clonal antigenic variation sensu stricto (Miller et al., 2002; Scherf et al., 2008) extends the duration of infection to facilitate transmission to the mosquito.
evidence: The introduction cites literature on the function of antigenic variation.

claim: Specific var genes are associated with severe malarial disease and specific PfEMP1 binding phenotypes.
source: Not only do var genes influence transmission, but specific var genes are associated with severe malarial disease and specific PfEMP1 binding phenotypes (Deitsch et al., 2009; Chan et al., 2012; Claessens et al., 2012; Lavstsen et al., 2012; Warimwe et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple studies on var gene associations with disease.

claim: Individual P. falciparum genomes have distinct repertoires of var genes.
source: Population studies have shown that individual P. falciparum genomes have distinct repertoires of var genes (Barry et al., 2007; Scherf et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2011) that extensively recombine (Freitas-Junior et al., 2000; Taylor et al., 2000) during sexual recombination in the mosquito (Paul et al., 1995).
evidence: The introduction cites population studies on var gene repertoires.

claim: Var genes extensively recombine during sexual recombination in the mosquito.
source: Population studies have shown that individual P. falciparum genomes have distinct repertoires of var genes (Barry et al., 2007; Scherf et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2011) that extensively recombine (Freitas-Junior et al., 2000; Taylor et al., 2000) during sexual recombination in the mosquito (Paul et al., 1995).
evidence: The introduction cites studies on var gene recombination.

claim: The immense sequence diversity observed among var genes and var repertoires has been attributed to high rates of meiotic (and possibly also mitotic) recombination.
source: The immense sequence diversity observed among var genes and var repertoires has been attributed to high rates of meiotic (and possibly also mitotic) recombination.
evidence: The introduction presents this as an established explanation.

claim: High rates of recombination presumably allow for very low linkage disequilibrium among var loci.
source: These high rates of recombination presumably allow for very low linkage disequilibrium among var loci.
evidence: The introduction presents this as a logical inference from high recombination rates.

claim: Only a few dominant var repertoires circulate and persist at any given time, despite the large potential diversity.
source: Despite this large potential diversity, simulation results show that only a few dominant var repertoires circulate and persist at any given time, effectively keeping var repertoire diversity orders of magnitude lower than is potentially possible given the number of var genes present in the host population (Figure 1).
evidence: The Results section presents simulation findings shown in Figure 1.

claim: Epidemiological dynamics significantly limit the diversity of coexisting dominant genomes under a broad spectrum of transmission intensities.
source: We find that epidemiological dynamics significantly limit the diversity of coexisting dominant genomes under a broad spectrum of transmission intensities.
evidence: The Results section presents this as a finding from the model.

claim: The pattern of limited diversity persists in the long-term, far out-living the influence of initial conditions.
source: This pattern persists in the long-term, far out-living the influence of initial conditions, and persisting through occasional changes in the identity of the dominant var repertoires (Figure 1).
evidence: The Results section describes the temporal dynamics shown in Figure 1.

claim: Most of the parasite population is structured into a limited number of distinct var repertoires on epidemiological and longer time scales.
source: Thus, on epidemiological (and longer) time scales, most of the parasite population is structured into a limited number of distinct var repertoires.
evidence: The Results section summarizes the model findings.

claim: The parasite population structure exhibits punctuated turnover with brief episodes of restructuring resulting in a new set of dominant var repertoires.
source: We find that the parasite population structure exhibits punctuated turnover: brief episodes of restructuring result in a new set of dominant var repertoires.
evidence: The Results section describes the dynamics observed in the model.

claim: Despite changing identities of dominant var repertoires, the overall diversity of repertoires present and individual gene frequencies remain remarkably constant.
source: Despite the changing identities of the dominant var repertoires, the overall diversity of repertoires present and the individual gene frequencies remain remarkably constant (Figure 1, lower panels).
evidence: The Results section describes patterns shown in Figure 1.

claim: Episodes of restructuring become more frequent as recombination rates increase, but the diversity of dominant var repertoires remains low throughout these semi-stable states.
source: The episodes of restructuring become more frequent as recombination rates increase, but the diversity of dominant var repertoires remains low throughout these semi-stable states.
evidence: The Results section describes the effect of recombination rate on dynamics.

claim: The maintenance of structure is robust even under very high levels of recombination.
source: Indeed, the maintenance of structure is found to be robust even under very high levels of recombination (Figure 1).
evidence: The Results section presents this finding with reference to Figure 1.

claim: The emergence of pathogen population structure is robust to alternative formulations of the multi-locus model that do not consider sequential expression.
source: The emergence of pathogen population structure is robust to alternative formulations of our multi-locus model that do not consider sequential expression, or formulations that consider randomly ordered sequential expression.
evidence: The Results section describes robustness tests of the model.

claim: As transmission intensity increases, the overlap between distinct dominant var repertoires increases.
source: However, as transmission intensity increases, the overlap between distinct dominant var repertoires also increases, with completely discordant genomes only appearing at the lower end of the spectrum (see Figure 2).
evidence: The Results section describes the relationship shown in Figure 2.

claim: As transmission intensity (biting rate) increases, all four measures (N*, V*, R*, F*) increase.
source: We find that as transmission intensity (biting rate) increases, all four measures increase as well, and that epidemiological dynamics clearly constrain var repertoire diversity and structure parasite populations, with the degree of overlap determined by epidemiological parameters (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: The Results section describes relationships shown in Figure 3.

claim: The findings are robust to different host population sizes (from 1,000 to 100,000 individuals), different gene pool sizes (from 10 to 500), and different repertoire lengths (from 2 to 30).
source: Our findings are robust to different host population sizes (from 1,000 to 100,000 individuals), different gene pools sizes (from 10 to 500), and different repertoire lengths (from 2 to 30) (Figure 3).
evidence: The Results section describes parameter sensitivity analyses shown in Figure 3.

claim: Areas that experience different transmission intensities will exhibit 'characteristic' epidemiological signatures.
source: The model suggests that areas that experience different transmission intensities will exhibit 'characteristic' epidemiological signatures (Figure 4).
evidence: The Results section presents model predictions shown in Figure 4.

claim: The gain of immunity depends on the degree of repertoire overlap (i.e., the number of shared var alleles) among the different dominant genomes and not just on total prevalence.
source: Importantly, the gain of immunity is found to depend on the degree of repertoire overlap (i.e., the number of shared var alleles) among the different dominant genomes and not just on total prevalence (Figure 5).
evidence: The Results section presents this finding with reference to Figure 5.

claim: The frequency distribution of distinct var genes is significantly different from what would be expected if sequence types were equal in frequency and uncorrelated.
source: These new data clearly show that the frequency distribution of distinct var genes, or sequence 'types' (defined by the level of sequence identity within the DBLα domain) is significantly different from what we would expect if sequence types were equal in frequency and uncorrelated (Figure 6).
evidence: The Results section presents empirical data analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The data show significant nonrandom associations among many var DBLα types within the sampled isolates.
source: In addition, the data show significant nonrandom associations among many var DBLα types within the sampled isolates (Figure 6).
evidence: The Results section presents empirical data analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The observed frequency distribution for var types is significantly different from the expected distribution when assuming all var types circulate at equal frequencies (pv<0.0001 using a K–S two sample test).
source: The observed distribution for the data (red) and the expected distribution when assuming all var types circulate at equal frequencies (blue) were found to be significantly different (pv<0.0001 using a K–S two sample test).
evidence: Figure 6 caption presents statistical test results.

claim: The co-occurrence of var types found in multiple isolates is significantly higher than for the null expectation under the assumption of linkage equilibrium among all var types (pv<0.01).
source: The co-occurrence of var types found in multiple isolates is significantly higher than for the null expectation under the assumption of linkage equilibrium among all var types (pv<0.01) (Artzy-Randrup and Stone, 2005) (the expected co-occurrence matrix conserves both the observed number of var types in each isolate and the observed frequency distribution of different var types (Chen et al., 2011)).
evidence: Figure 6 caption presents statistical test results with citation.

claim: Var DBLα repertoire relatedness is not a function of microsatellite repertoire relatedness.
source: Another important observation is that, at least at this level of resolution, var DBLα repertoire relatedness is not a function of microsatellite repertoire relatedness.
evidence: The Results section presents this as an empirical observation.

claim: The D values of the var DBLα dataset are higher than those of the microsatellite dataset (pv<<0.0001 by Mann–Whitney test).
source: The D values of the var DBLα dataset are higher than those of the microsatellite dataset (pv<<0.0001 by Mann–Whitney test), and we argue that this cannot easily be explained by allele frequency differences or differences in the extent of physical linkage among sites (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: The Results section presents statistical comparison of datasets.

claim: For the var DBLα dataset there are 1288 distinct pairs of alleles with positive D values that exceed a two-tailed significance threshold of 0.05.
source: For the var DBLα dataset there are 1288 distinct pairs of alleles with positive D values that exceed a two-tailed significance threshold of 0.05 (Hedrick et al., 1978).
evidence: The Results section presents statistical analysis with citation.

claim: Under the null hypothesis of no significant correlations between alleles, only 310 pairs would be expected to exceed the significance threshold for var DBLα.
source: Given the number of tests performed, under the null hypothesis of no significant correlations between alleles, we would expect only 310 pairs to exceed this threshold.
evidence: The Results section presents expected values under null hypothesis.

claim: For the microsatellite dataset there are 146 distinct pairs of alleles with positive D values that exceed the significance threshold.
source: For the microsatellite dataset there are 146 distinct pairs of alleles with positive D values that exceed the significance threshold and under the null hypothesis we would expect only 49.
evidence: The Results section presents statistical analysis.

claim: Both var DBLα and microsatellite datasets show an enrichment of positive correlations among allele pairs, and thus, significant linkage disequilibrium.
source: Therefore, both datasets show an enrichment of positive correlations among allele pairs, and thus, significant linkage disequilibrium.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the statistical analyses.

claim: The model constrains total repertoire diversity to levels that are orders of magnitude lower than is potentially possible given the diversity of the gene pool.
source: In accordance with predictions from the original 'strain theory', our model constrains total repertoire diversity to levels that are orders of magnitude lower than is potentially possible given the diversity of the gene pool.
evidence: The Discussion summarizes the main finding.

claim: This reduction in diversity occurs because coexisting parasites are structured into a few variants with largely discordant repertoires.
source: This reduction in diversity occurs because coexisting parasites are structured into a few variants with largely discordant repertoires.
evidence: The Discussion explains the mechanism behind the finding.

claim: The model predicts that different dominant repertoires can exhibit partial overlap, and the extent of the overlap increases with transmission intensity.
source: In a departure from previous strain theory, our model predicts that the different dominant repertoires can exhibit partial overlap; the extent of the overlap increases with transmission intensity and this, in turn, influences observed epidemiological patterns (particularly age-serology profiles).
evidence: The Discussion presents this as a novel prediction from the model.

claim: The specific immune profile of each individual host effectively structures the population into distinct sets of 'patches' or 'resources' that define an immune environment, ultimately causing immune selection to act on the parasite population.
source: The specific immune profile of each individual host effectively structures the population into distinct sets of 'patches' or 'resources' that define an immune environment, ultimately causing immune selection to act on the parasite population.
evidence: The Discussion explains the mechanism of immune selection in the model.

claim: Discordant repertoires that exhibit partial immunological/antigenic overlap blur the distinction between the acquisition of strictly strain-specific immunity and the acquisition of strictly strain-transcending immunity.
source: Discordant repertoires that exhibit partial immunological/antigenic overlap blur the distinction between the acquisition of strictly strain-specific immunity and the acquisition of strictly strain-transcending immunity (Gupta and Day, 1994a, 1994b) (see caption of Figure 5).
evidence: The Discussion presents this as an implication of the model with citation.

claim: By reducing antigenic overlap between strains, vector control efforts will result in infection at an older age and a more gradual acquisition of protection to infection, even in the absence of changes in var gene diversity.
source: By reducing antigenic overlap between strains, vector control efforts will result in infection at an older age and a more gradual acquisition of protection to infection, even in the absence of changes in var gene diversity.
evidence: The Discussion presents this as a prediction from the model.

claim: Decreasing transmission provokes nonlinear changes in the dominant var configurations.
source: Our models support this proposal as they show that decreasing transmission provokes nonlinear changes in the dominant var configurations.
evidence: The Discussion presents this as a model finding.

claim: Vector control strategies that reduce transmission will not always drastically reduce var gene diversity, because a reservoir of parasite genomes with diverse (highly non-overlapping) var repertoires will remain.
source: Importantly, our results demonstrate that there is not a simple relationship between var diversity and repertoire diversity. Indeed, the 'var strain' model suggests that vector control strategies that reduce transmission will not always drastically reduce var gene diversity, because a reservoir of parasite genomes with diverse (highly non-overlapping) var repertoires will remain.
evidence: The Discussion presents this as an implication of the model.

claim: Non-overlapping var diversity will create significant inherent difficulties in reducing the potential of the malaria parasite to reinfect the same hosts.
source: This insight from the model provides a plausible explanation for why it is so difficult to eliminate malaria: non-overlapping var diversity will create significant inherent difficulties in reducing the potential of the malaria parasite to reinfect the same hosts.
evidence: The Discussion presents this as an inference from the model.

claim: The results have broad implications for the possible emergence of similar structure in many important human and animal pathogens that have major surface antigens encoded by multigene families, including bacterial, protozoan and fungal pathogens.
source: In conclusion, the results of our model on the dynamics of population structure in P. falciparum as defined by the var multi-gene family, have broad implications for the possible emergence of similar structure in many important human and animal pathogens that have major surface antigens encoded by multigene families, including bacterial, protozoan and fungal pathogens (Deitsch et al., 2009).
evidence: The Discussion presents this as a broader implication with citation.

claim: Each parasite is composed of a set of exactly g var genes.
source: Each parasite is composed of a set of exactly g var genes, and the genomes are distinguishable from each other by their unique var combination.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model structure.

claim: The overall diversity of var genes circulating in the host population is assumed to originate from a general predefined pool of G variants.
source: The overall diversity of var genes circulating in the host population is assumed to originate from a general predefined pool of G variants (Barry et al., 2007; Chen et al., 2011; Recker et al., 2011).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption with citations.

claim: The total number of distinct var repertoires is G!/(G-g)!.
source: Hence, the total number of distinct var repertoires is G!/(G-g)!.
evidence: The Materials and methods section presents this mathematical relationship.

claim: During the course of an infection, a parasite expresses all of its var genes, which are responsible for encoding PfEMP1 variant surface antigens (VSAs).
source: During the course of an infection, a parasite expresses all of its var genes, and these are responsible for encoding PfEMP1 variant surface antigens (VSAs) (Gupta et al., 1994; Miller et al., 2002; Scherf et al., 2008; Tibayrenc and Ayala, 2002).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model with citations.

claim: After the host is exposed to each VSA, it gains life-long immunity that is specific to each of the antigens.
source: After the host is exposed to each of these VSAs, it gains life-long immunity that is specific to each of the antigens (Bull et al., 1998; Recker et al., 2011).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption with citations.

claim: The total duration of infection in a susceptible host lasts a fixed time (κyrs.).
source: We assume that the total duration of infection in a susceptible host lasts a fixed time (κyrs.), and that in partially immune hosts, the actual duration decreases proportionally to the number of var genes that have been expressed in earlier infections (Bruce et al., 2000a, 2000b; Giha et al., 2000).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption with citations.

claim: In partially immune hosts, the actual duration of infection decreases proportionally to the number of var genes that have been expressed in earlier infections.
source: We assume that the total duration of infection in a susceptible host lasts a fixed time (κyrs.), and that in partially immune hosts, the actual duration decreases proportionally to the number of var genes that have been expressed in earlier infections (Bruce et al., 2000a, 2000b; Giha et al., 2000).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption with citations.

claim: The var genes composing an infecting parasite are mutually and exclusively expressed in a fixed sequential order.
source: It is recognized that the gain of immunity during the course of an infection is gradual (Ewers, 1972; Miller et al., 1994), and we capture this feature by considering that the var genes composing an infecting parasite are mutually and exclusively expressed in a fixed sequential order.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption with citations.

claim: An infected host can harbor multiple simultaneously co-infecting parasite genomes.
source: An infected host can harbor multiple simultaneously co-infecting parasite genomes, and each has the potential of being transmitted to another host through a mosquito biting event.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model structure.

claim: When a biting event takes place, each of the infecting parasites has a probability, τ, of successfully being transmitted from the infected host to the mosquito.
source: When such an event takes place, each of the infecting parasites has a probability, τ, of successfully being transmitted from the infected host to the mosquito, making it possible for several different genomes to be transmitted in a single biting event (see Figure 7A).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: The actual transmission probability of each genome is divided by the total number of co-infecting genomes at the time of the biting event.
source: However, in our model we assume that the actual transmission probability of each of the genomes, is divided by the total number of co-infecting genomes at the time of the biting event.
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption.

claim: There is a cost to co-infection that is consistent with empirical evidence for a density-dependent regulating mechanism on parasite abundance within the host.
source: Therefore, in effect, there is a cost to co-infection that is consistent with empirical evidence for a density-dependent regulating mechanism on parasite abundance within the host (Bruce et al., 2000a, 2000b; Bruce and Day, 2002, 2003) (see Figure 7B).
evidence: The Materials and methods section describes the model assumption with citations and reference to Figure 7B.

claim: DBLα is the most informative molecular marker of var gene diversity because it is the only domain found in nearly all PfEMP1 variants.
source: Because DBLα is the only domain found in nearly all PfEMP1 variants (Miller et al., 2002), the sequence encoding the central portion of this domain provides the most informative molecular marker of var gene diversity (Freitas-Junior et al., 2000; Taylor et al., 2000; Barry et al., 2007; Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the rationale with citations.

claim: Two DBLα tags are considered to represent two distinct var 'types' if their nucleotide sequence identity is less than 96%.
source: Two DBLα tags are considered to represent two distinct var 'types' if their nucleotide sequence identity is less than 96%.
evidence: The Materials and methods section defines the classification criterion.

claim: Microsatellites offer an ideal and practical means to construct a null hypothesis reflecting the demographic forces shaping diversity because these sites are predominantly neutral.
source: Microsatellites offer an ideal and practical means to construct a null hypothesis reflecting the demographic forces shaping diversity because these sites are predominantly neutral, and their diversity can be explained by a mechanism unrelated to immune selection (i.e., slippage).
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the rationale for using microsatellites.

claim: D is maximized when allele frequencies are 0.5.
source: D is maximized when allele frequencies are 0.5, so D also indicates the amount of information upon which the coefficient is based (e.g., if two alleles appear only once and in the same isolate, their D will be low despite the fact that they are in perfect correlation with one another).
evidence: The Materials and methods section explains the properties of the D statistic.

claim: The higher D values for var DBLα alleles versus microsatellite alleles cannot be attributed to differences in allele frequencies since the var DBLα alleles have lower frequencies than the microsatellite alleles.
source: The higher D values for var DBLα alleles versus microsatellite alleles cannot be attributed to differences in allele frequencies since the var DBLα alleles have lower frequencies than the microsatellite alleles, and thus, D values biased to lower magnitudes.
evidence: The Materials and methods section presents this argument.

claim: The great majority of var loci are located very far from other var loci in the 3D7 genome.
source: While the higher D values from the var DBLα dataset could be due to the influence of the close physical linkage of a small subset of pairs of var loci (Deitsch and Hviid, 2004), it seems somewhat unlikely because the great majority of var loci are located very far from other var loci in the 3D7 genome (Deitsch and Hviid, 2004), and var loci have been shown to coincide with recombination hotspots (Mu et al., 2010; Jiang et al., 2011) in a genome that is already characterized by remarkably high underlying rates of recombination (Conway et al., 1999; Volkman et al., 2006).
evidence: The Materials and methods section cites literature on var loci distribution.

claim: Var loci have been shown to coincide with recombination hotspots.
source: While the higher D values from the var DBLα dataset could be due to the influence of the close physical linkage of a small subset of pairs of var loci (Deitsch and Hviid, 2004), it seems somewhat unlikely because the great majority of var loci are located very far from other var loci in the 3D7 genome (Deitsch and Hviid, 2004), and var loci have been shown to coincide with recombination hotspots (Mu et al., 2010; Jiang et al., 2011) in a genome that is already characterized by remarkably high underlying rates of recombination (Conway et al., 1999; Volkman et al., 2006).
evidence: The Materials and methods section cites literature on var loci and recombination.

claim: The P. falciparum genome is characterized by remarkably high underlying rates of recombination.
source: While the higher D values from the var DBLα dataset could be due to the influence of the close physical linkage of a small subset of pairs of var loci (Deitsch and Hviid, 2004), it seems somewhat unlikely because the great majority of var loci are located very far from other var loci in the 3D7 genome (Deitsch and Hviid, 2004), and var loci have been shown to coincide with recombination hotspots (Mu et al., 2010; Jiang et al., 2011) in a genome that is already characterized by remarkably high underlying rates of recombination (Conway et al., 1999; Volkman et al., 2006).
evidence: The Materials and methods section cites literature on P. falciparum recombination rates.
